findings.description: Hover effect implementation unclear: the explanation about transform order is technically correct but confusing. 'CSS transforms apply in reverse order (last specified, first applied)' is accurate, but 'original Y-axis' is misleading. TranslateY operates on the already transformed coordinate system, not a hypothetical 'original' axis.
findings.fix: Replace the current explanation with: 'CSS transforms are applied right-to-left. So scale(1.1) rotate(2deg) translateY(-4px) means: (1) translateY moves the element first, (2) rotate turns the translated result around its center, (3) scale enlarges the rotated result. The final visual is: element lifts 4px, rotates 2°, then grows by 10%.'

findings.location: 02-design.md, Edge Cases, Touch Devices, Implementation Steps
findings.description: No JavaScript for copy-to-clipboard touch interaction: the design assumes 'On touch devices, tapping .cor-item copies the color value to clipboard' with visual feedback, but there is zero JavaScript in natal.html that handles .cor-item taps. The only JS in the file controls music playback.
findings.fix: Either (a) remove the clipboard behavior from the design if out of scope, or (b) specify minimal JS in the design: 'Add a click handler for .cor-item elements that calls navigator.clipboard.writeText(colorValue) and briefly applies .active class (e.g., transform: scale(1.1) translateY(-4px); transition: transform 0.15s ease;) for touch feedback.'

findings.description: Contrast risk for dark background swatch (--texto): The .cor-item with background var(--texto) (#5c5652) uses white text (color:#fff) with text-shadow:0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,.3). The text-shadow darkens the text edges, worsening contrast. Contrast ratio for white text on #5c5652 is ~3.1:1, which fails WCAG AA (minimum 4.5:1 for normal text).
findings.fix: Specify a concrete solution in the design: 'For .cor-item with dark background (#5c5652), override text styling: .paleta .cor-item.dark .cor-valor, .paleta .cor-item.dark .cor-nome { color:#fff; text-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.6); }' OR use '-webkit-text-stroke: 0.5px #2a2522;' to increase legibility while keeping color:#fff.'

findings.description: prefers-reduced-motion media query missing implementation scope: the design proposes adding prefers-reduced-motion: reduce but does not clarify whether all transitions (e.g., transition: transform .25s ease, box-shadow .25s ease on .cor-item) should be disabled or only the hover effects.
findings.fix: Add to the design: 'When prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, disable all animations: .paleta .cor-item { transition: none; } .paleta .cor-item:hover { transform: none; box-shadow: none; }'

findings.description: Touch feedback visual state not specified: the design says touch tap shows 'brief scale-up via transform: scale(1.1) translateY(-4px) without rotation', but CSS only has a hover state. There is no :active or .active class defined for touch feedback, so hover and tap effects would be identical in code, causing confusion.
findings.fix: Add to the design: 'Define separate visual states: - Hover: .paleta .cor-item:hover { transform: scale(1.1) rotate(2deg) translateY(-4px); } - Active (touch): .paleta .cor-item:active { transform: scale(1.05) translateY(-2px); } This ensures touch feedback is subtle and distinct.'

findings.description: z-index: 1 alone may not prevent overlay clipping: .cor-item has overflow:hidden. When scaled by 1.1, content may be clipped by the border-radius. z-index: 1 on overlays does not fix clipping.
findings.fix: Add to the design: 'Two options to prevent clipping: (a) Remove overflow:hidden from .cor-item and keep border-radius:14px only on the parent, or (b) Add padding to .cor-item to accommodate the 10% scale growth (e.g., padding:10px instead of relying on absolute-positioned overlays).'
